clauses.reason: The sole paragraph orders that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. Revocation is complete when the order takes effect, which is the signing date, April 21, 1948 (the filing stamp on the page also reads April 21, 1948). The command was exhausted by performance on that date; the end source is the order's own text. No earlier or later date is supported.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9950 (13 FR 2191 (Federal Register of April 23, 1948)) was signed April 21, 1948. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 21, 1948. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence ordering that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on April 21, 1948. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page of April 23, 1948 that reproduces this same order together with Executive Order 9951 (EO_9951.txt); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947, which prescribed the functions of the armed forces remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
